intro: What a person is like: personality adjectives, their opposites and expressions with «carácter».
p.carácter.consejo: The accent shows the stress: ca-RÁC-ter. In the plural the stress moves: «caracteres», ca-rac-TE-res.
p.sincero.consejo: It changes with gender: «sincero», «sincera». The noun is «la sinceridad».
p.paciente.consejo: It works for a boy and for a girl: «un chico paciente», «una chica paciente».
p.impaciente.consejo: It is the opposite of «paciente». Before p, the prefix in- is written im-.
p.inseguro.consejo: It is «seguro» with the prefix in-, which gives the opposite meaning: «seguro», «inseguro».
p.introvertido.consejo: The v sounds like b: in-tro-ber-TI-do. Its opposite is «extrovertido».
p.hablador.consejo: The h is silent. It ends in -or and the stress is last: a-bla-DOR. Feminine: «habladora».
p.travieso.consejo: It is said mostly about children. The v sounds like b: tra-BYE-so.
p.maleducado.consejo: It is «mal» + «educado». The opposite is «educado»: he says «por favor» and «gracias».
p.paciencia.consejo: It comes from «paciente»: the adjective ends in -nte and the noun in -ncia.
p.sentido del humor.consejo: The h of «humor» is silent: u-MOR. You say «tener sentido del humor».
p.portarse bien.consejo: Its opposite is «portarse mal». The pronoun changes: «me porto bien», «se portan bien».
p.parecerse a.glosa: to look like, to take after
p.parecerse a.consejo: It always takes «a» before the person: «se parece a su padre».
p.en cambio.consejo: It joins two opposite ideas: «Marta habla poco; Elena, en cambio, habla mucho».
b1.texto:
To describe character we use **ser** + adjective: Marta **es sincera**, Elena **es habladora**.

Many adjectives have an opposite made with a prefix:

- **paciente → impaciente** (before p, in- becomes im-)
- **seguro → inseguro**
- **educado → maleducado**

There are also expressions with **carácter**: **tener mucho carácter** (to be strong and determined) and **tener mal carácter** (to get angry easily). **Tener sentido del humor** means knowing how to laugh.

With **parecerse a** we talk about inherited traits: Elena **se parece a** su padre. And with **portarse bien / mal**, about how a person behaves.
b2.f0.texto: Do your two daughters look alike?
b2.f2.texto: Marta is introverted and very patient.
b2.f3.texto: She looks a lot like her father.
b2.f5.texto: Elena is talkative, impatient and a bit naughty.
b2.f6.texto: She has a strong personality and a great sense of humour.
b2.f7.texto: Do the two of them behave well at school?
b2.f8.texto: Both are polite and never treat anyone badly.
b4.texto:
Opposites are formed in several ways:

- **in- / im-**: seguro → **in**seguro · paciente → **im**paciente
- **des-**: agradable → **des**agradable
- **mal-**: educado → **mal**educado

With **ser** we say what a person is always like: Marta **es** paciente. With **estar**, how they feel right now: today she **está** impaciente.

The adjective agrees with the person: Marta es introvertid**a** · Pablo es introvertid**o**.
b4.e0.texto: Marta is patient, but today she is impatient.
b4.e1.texto: My brother is polite and never behaves badly.
b4.e2.texto: A rude person treats their classmates badly.
b5.f0.texto: Marta sits by the window with an open book on her knees.
b5.f1.texto: Her silence has the calm colour of an afternoon without wind.
b5.f2.texto: When someone calls her, she slowly looks up and smiles shyly.
b5.f3.texto: Her hands arrange the pencils with the calm of a gardener.
b5.f4.texto: Her patience seems like a lake where time is in no hurry.
b5.f5.texto: Elena comes into the house like a summer storm.
b5.f6.texto: She talks without stopping, laughs out loud and drops her backpack on the floor.
b5.f7.texto: Her voice fills the house with noise and light.
b5.f8.texto: One afternoon she hides her sister's shoes under the sofa.
b5.f9.texto: Marta looks at her, sighs and gives her back a smile of patience.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Maleducado» is the opposite of «educado», not of «paciente».
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: paciente → impaciente. Before p, the prefix in- is written im-.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Inseguro» is the opposite of «seguro». Find the one that fits «paciente».
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Parecerse» does not use «de». Check the rule: se parece a su padre.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Con» means company. To look like someone you use «a».
b7.o2.refuerzo: Well done! «Parecerse» always takes «a»: se parece a su padre.
b7.pregunta: Marta is just like her father. What is missing?
b8.frase: Elena tiene un gran sentido del humor
b8.traduccion: Elena has a great sense of humour
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it! Someone who never says thanks has bad manners: he is maleducado.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Educado» is the opposite: he says «gracias» and «por favor».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Sincero» tells the truth. It has nothing to do with manners.
b9.pregunta: He never says «thanks» or «please». What is he like?
b11.frase: Marta suele ser paciente, pero hoy ____ impaciente.
b11.o0.refuerzo: «Es» says what someone is always like. Here we talk about «hoy»: a state right now.
b11.o1.refuerzo: That's it! «Estar» says how she feels today; «ser», what she is always like.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Tener» does not join an adjective like this. You say «está impaciente».
b11.pregunta: Today Marta has no patience. Which verb is missing?
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Hablador» talks a lot; Pablo talks little. It is the opposite.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Travieso» plays pranks. It has nothing to do with talking little.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Well done! Someone who talks little and prefers to be alone is introvertido.
b12.pregunta: Pablo talks little and prefers to be alone. What is he like?
p.hijas.consejo: The h is silent: I-has. The singular is «hija»; the masculine plural «hijos» can mean children.
p.introvertida.consejo: Feminine of «introvertido». The v sounds like b: in-tro-ber-TI-da.
p.habladora.consejo: Feminine of «hablador». The h is silent: a-bla-DO-ra.
p.traviesa.consejo: Feminine of «travieso». The «ie» is a single sound and the v sounds like b: tra-BYE-sa.
p.portan.consejo: Form of «portarse»: «se portan bien» means «they behave well».
p.educadas.consejo: Feminine plural of «educado». It is the opposite of «maleducado».
p.tratan.consejo: Form of «tratar». With «mal» or «bien» it says how someone treats a person: «tratan mal a alguien».
p.porta.consejo: Form of «portarse». It is not the noun «la puerta»: «se porta mal» is about behaviour.
p.trata.consejo: Form of «tratar». «Trata mal a sus compañeros» means he treats classmates badly.
p.llama.consejo: Form of «llamar». The ll sounds like y: YA-ma. Here it means to call someone.
p.vista.consejo: The v sounds like b: BIS-ta. «Levantar la vista» means to look up.
p.ordenan.consejo: Form of «ordenar», from «orden». It can also mean to order someone to do something.
p.jardinero.consejo: The j sounds like h: har-di-NE-ro. Feminine: «jardinera». It comes from «jardín».
p.lago.consejo: The g is hard because it comes before a: LA-go. It is masculine: «el lago».
p.carcajadas.consejo: Almost always plural. «Reír a carcajadas» means to laugh out loud.
p.mochila.consejo: The ch sounds as in «chocolate»: mo-CHI-la. It is feminine: «la mochila».
p.esconde.consejo: Form of «esconder». The c sounds k: es-KON-de. The opposite is «encontrar».
p.suspira.consejo: Form of «suspirar»; the noun is «el suspiro». The s sounds like in «sun».
p.devuelve.consejo: Form of «devolver»: the o becomes «ue». The v sounds like b: de-BWEL-be.
